question: How many first-place votes will the winner of the 2026 National League MVP Award receive?

calls.reasoning: Base rate: winners who swept MLB.com's final expert poll (Acuña 2023, Ohtani 2023-25, Judge 2024) got 30/30 first-place votes in BBWAA voting; Judge 2022 got 28, losing 2 to Ohtani's two-way case. PCA had a historic season: 10.6 fWAR (leads MLB by ~3.7), 45 HR and 41 SB, NL-best OPS. He took all 38 first-place votes in MLB.com's final poll, won the Players Choice awards, and Polymarket has him at 0.99 to win. Counter: finalist Ohtani has a real two-way case (1.79 ERA in 85.2 IP plus 30 HR, 142 wRC+) and could draw 1-3 first-place votes from loyal voters, as in 2022. Schwarber, who tied for the HR lead but slumped late, is a minor threat. Market check: Polymarket and Kalshi only price who wins, not the vote count, so they are evidence about the winner, not an anchor; no vote-count market found. Rough distribution: P(30) ~0.55-0.6, P(29) ~0.18, P(28) ~0.09, P(27 or fewer) ~0.15, including a tiny upset tail.
calls.dossier:
- MLB.com final 2026 MVP poll (Sept 22; fetched this run): Crow-Armstrong got all 38 first-place votes and 190 points. Ohtani 135, Misiorowski and De La Cruz 61 each, Schwarber 32.
- MLB.com poll text: Ohtani played only 3 games in September (knee and biceps injuries) and did not pitch the rest of the season. Final line: 1.79 ERA, 95 K in 85.2 IP; 30 HR, 142 wRC+ at the plate. So Ohtani DID pitch in 2026, contrary to the question's background text.
- Wikipedia and search snippets (Oct-Nov 2026): PCA hit .280 with 45 HR, 107 RBI and 41 SB in 162 games. 10.6 fWAR, leading MLB in both major WAR versions; next-best position player was Witt at 6.9 fWAR. NL-best .942 OPS, NL lead in runs, 40-40 club.
- Search snippet: NL MVP finalists are Crow-Armstrong, Ohtani and Schwarber. Schwarber tied PCA for the MLB HR lead at 45 but went 4-for-34 with 1 HR over his last 10 games as of the final poll.
- Yardbarker (Oct 2026): PCA beat Ohtani for the Players Choice NL Outstanding Player award and also won MLB Player of the Year.
- Fox Sports and Yahoo: sportsbooks had PCA at -10000 before pulling the market.
- Win markets (Polymarket, Kalshi) price only who wins, not the first-place vote count. No vote-count market found.
- Reference class, MLB.com final-poll sweepers and their BBWAA first-place votes: 2023 Acuña 30/30, 2023 Ohtani AL 30/30, 2024 Ohtani 30/30, 2024 Judge 30/30, 2025 Ohtani 30/30. 2022 Judge 28/30 (2 went to two-way Ohtani).
- Broader class, all NL winners 2019-2025: 19, 28, 17, 22, 30, 30, 30. The non-sweep years were contested races.
- Resolves off the BBWAA ballot breakdown at bbwaa.com, not media polls. Ballots were cast before the postseason, so October results are irrelevant.
- Event window: ballots cast late Sept/early Oct 2026, announced Nov 12, 2026. As of Nov 2 the voting is finished and only the announcement remains.
- Searched but not found: any leaked or individual writer ballots, any market on the first-place vote count, and Ohtani's combined bWAR.

calls.reasoning: Crow-Armstrong is a ~99% favorite (Kalshi and Polymarket winner markets at 99%; those contracts are on who wins, not the vote count, so they're evidence, not an anchor). He had 10.6 fWAR (MLB-leading), 45 HR (tied for the MLB lead), 41 SB and a .942 OPS, and won all 38 first-place votes in MLB.com's final poll. Runaway NL MVPs have been unanimous recently (2023-2025), while Freeman in 2020 got 28. The main risk is a few writers putting Ohtani first for his two-way season (30 HR, .889 OPS, 85.2 IP at a 1.79 ERA), or a stray vote for Misiorowski or De La Cruz. Ohtani's mid-September injury and his move away from pitching weaken his case. Median about 30; meaningful mass at 27-29.

calls.reasoning: Crow-Armstrong is a ~99% winner (Polymarket 0.99, finalist, swept all 38 first-place votes in MLB.com's final poll, MLB-leading 10.6 fWAR, 45 HR/41 SB, Players Choice POY). Reference class of final-poll sweepers 2022-2025: 5 of 6 got 30/30; Judge 2022 got 28 because of Ohtani's full two-way season. Ohtani's 2026 two-way case (85.2 IP at 1.79 ERA, 30 HR, injured in September) is real but weaker than in 2022, so a 1-2 vote leak is the main downside; Schwarber is a minor risk. P(30)≈0.63.
calls.reconciliation: Factual: the question background says Ohtani didn't pitch; all three dossiers cite MLB.com showing 85.2 IP with a 1.79 ERA. I accept that he pitched, which makes Ohtani a plausible source of contrarian first-place votes, though weaker than in 2022. The finalists (PCA, Ohtani, Schwarber) come from one search snippet in Run 1 and are not contradicted. All runs agree on PCA's stats, the poll sweep, and that no vote-count market exists. What remains is judgment about how many votes leak. Given the WAR gap and the 5/6 unanimity rate among poll sweepers, I put P(30) slightly above the runs' 0.55-0.60. I carry forward a dispersion similar to Run 1's.

disagreements.claim: Ohtani did not pitch in 2026 (question background) vs. he pitched 85.2 IP (dossiers)
disagreements.verdict: All three dossiers independently cite MLB.com stats showing he pitched; accepted. The background text is wrong.
Set ~0.63: the reference class is 5/6 unanimous, and Ohtani's case is weaker than in 2022's lone exception.
